papers.title: Exchange rights and vacancy priorities
papers.title_ja: 交換権と空き席優先権
summary_ja: 在職者の位置交換と優先権に基づく空き席配分を行う配分制度を分析。
衝突サイクルのない方針において、交換権と優先権を守る耐戦略的ルールを解明。
提示・取引ルールを提案し、衝突のない方針の下で申請者最適コア配分を選択することを示す。
papers.reason_ja: マッチング理論における優先権・交換権と耐戦略性の整合性を扱うため。
papers.abstract: Many institutions let incumbents exchange positions while allocating announced vacancies by priority, withdrawing positions released by vacancy recipients. A policy specifies permitted exchanges, vacancy eligibility, and priorities. A strategy-proof, individually rational rule protecting exchange rights and vacancy priorities exists precisely for policies without conflict cycles. Restricting protection to first choices does not enlarge this class. We introduce the propose-and-trade rule, which satisfies these properties and selects the applicant-optimal core allocation under every conflict-free policy. We identify when propose-and-trade is the unique strategy-proof, individually rational rule protecting first choices. These axioms characterize deferred acceptance and top trading cycles in their classic settings. Under a policy with a conflict cycle, propose-and-trade is manipulable but protects exchange rights and first-choice claims. Replacing it with any strategy-proof rule makes some applicant worse off at some profile. We show when priority reform alone can eliminate conflict cycles and when eligibility or exchange permissions must change.

papers.title: Recognizing $k$-inducible Digraphs is NP-complete
papers.title_ja: k-誘導可能有向グラフの認識判定はNP完全である
summary_ja: k人の投票者の多数決関係に対応するk-誘導可能有向グラフの判定問題を研究。
トーナメントの3-誘導可能性判定、および固定されたk≥3での判定がNP完全と証明。
P≠NPの仮定下で、k-誘導可能有向グラフは有限個の禁止誘導部分グラフで特徴付けできない。
papers.reason_ja: 投票理論における多数決グラフの理論的複雑性と表現可能性を論じているため。
papers.abstract: A digraph is k-inducible if its arcs correspond to the pairwise majority relation of a preference profile with k voters. By McGarvey's theorem, every asymmetric digraph is k-inducible for some k, but for every fixed k there are digraphs that are not k-inducible. Whether a digraph is 1-inducible or 2-inducible can easily be decided in polynomial time. The complexity of deciding whether a digraph is k-inducible for every fixed $k\geq 3$ has been a long-standing open problem. We prove that deciding whether a tournament is 3-inducible is NP-complete and then leverage this result to show that deciding whether a digraph is k-inducible is NP-complete for every fixed $k\geq 3$. Our results imply that, unless P=NP, k-inducible digraphs cannot be characterized by finitely many forbidden induced subdigraphs.

papers.title: Decision Theory with Degree of Membership in the State Space
papers.title_ja: 状態空間における所属度を考慮した意思決定理論
summary_ja: 状態の可能性を2値とする伝統的枠組みに対し、ファジィ集合論の所属度概念を導入。
状態空間の構成自体に対する不確実性を定量的に表現する意思決定理論を展開。
主観的期待効用最大化、ミニマックス・リグレット、極大最小基準へ理論を拡張。
papers.reason_ja: 状態空間の不確実性を捉える新たな意思決定基準の公理化に関わるため。
papers.abstract: Classical decision theory considers a decision maker (DM) who faces a choice set C and believes that the true state of nature s* lies in a state space S. An objective function w(., .): C x S -> R1 maps actions and states into welfare. The DM wants to maximize w(., s*) but does not know s*. The state space specifies a labeled set of possible states. Possibility is binary: every state in S is possible and no state outside of S is possible. Thinking that this binary perspective on possibility is too rigid, we generalize the classical theory. We begin with a universe of labeled states U and a residual unlabeled state r. Classical theory associates a binary possibility indicator mu(s) with each s in (U, r). The residual state r is not possible, so mu(r) = 0. The state space is S = [s in U: mu(s) = 1]. We expand the range of mu to be the interval [0, 1]. Thus, mu is now a real number measuring degree of membership, a term we adopt from fuzzy set theory. The membership function mu(.): (U, r) -> [0, 1] differs substantively from but is consistent with the subjective probability distributions of Bayesian decision theory. Bayesian theory places a subjective distribution on the elements of a classical state space, each of whose members has degree of membership one. Degree of membership expresses the distinct idea that a DM may want to quantitatively express uncertainty regarding the composition of the state space. A mathematical distinction between subjective probabilities and degrees of membership is that the former must sum to one, but the latter need not. After formalizing basic ideas, we extend three prominent classical decision criteria--maximization of subjective expected welfare, minimax regret, and maximin--to our generalization of classical decision theory.

papers.title: Type-anonymity and strategy-proofness in a domain of single-peaked and single-dipped preferences
papers.title_ja: 単峰型および単谷型選好のドメインにおけるタイプ匿名性と耐戦略性
summary_ja: タイトルに基づき、単峰型と単谷型が混在する選好ドメインでのメカニズムを考察。
参加者のタイプに関する匿名性（タイプ匿名性）と耐戦略性の同時充足性を分析。
当該選好領域において両公理を満たす社会選択ルールの構造を解明していると推測される。
papers.reason_ja: 複合的な選好ドメインにおける配分ルールの公理的特徴付けを扱うため。

papers.title: Incentive Compatible Mechanisms for Sequential Fair Resource Allocation with Private Demands
papers.title_ja: 私的需要を伴う順次公平資源配分における誘因整合的メカニズム
summary_ja: 需要が私的情報であるエージェントへの分割可能資源の順次的・公平な配分を研究。
戦略的偽報が存在する状況で、誘因整合的配分ルールの構造と最適メカニズムを特定。
離散化動的計画法を有向非巡回グラフ上の最長経路問題へ帰着する近似法を提案。
papers.reason_ja: 動的な公平配分問題における耐戦略性とメカニズムデザインを扱うため。
papers.abstract: We study a strategic variant of the canonical online fair allocation problem, where a planner must sequentially allocate a divisible resource to agents with privately known demands. At each stage, the planner announces an allocation rule, the agent reports their demand, and the planner allocates resources according to the rule and the reported demand. Unlike the standard model, we allow agents to strategically misreport their needs, as can arise in nonprofit settings where demand is self-reported and monetary transfers are unavailable. We characterize the structure of incentive-compatible (IC) allocation rules in this model, and use this to identify conditions under which the optimal mechanism has a simple cap structure. We then develop an approximation method for the optimal IC mechanism through a careful reduction of the discretized dynamic program to a longest-path problem on a directed acyclic graph. Numerical experiments show that ignoring strategic reporting can be substantially more costly than imposing incentive compatibility.

papers.title: A Characterized Softmax for Distributing Standing Across Multiple Affiliations
papers.title_ja: 複数所属への立ち位置配分のための特徴付けられたソフトマックス
summary_ja: プレイヤーが重なりを持つ複数のグループに所属する際の属性帰属問題を定式化。
符号が混在するシグナル下で比率方式が無効となることを示し、制限領域ソフトマックスを提案。
5つの要件により温度パラメータを持つ一意の写像として解を公理的に特徴付け。
papers.reason_ja: 協力ゲーム理論における新たな帰属問題とその公理的解決策を提示するため。
papers.abstract: Cooperative game theory answers canonical questions on payoff allocation (Shapley, Owen), interaction attribution (Grabisch-Roubens, Faith-Shap), and coalition formation and stability. None answers a fourth question that arises whenever players carry known, overlapping group tags fixed independently of the game: how should a player's standing be distributed across the groups it already belongs to? We call this membership attribution, formalize it, and give a complete characterization of its solution. The direct, ratio-based answer is provably invalid whenever a player's group-level signals have mixed sign --- a common, structurally unavoidable case. We propose a restricted-domain softmax construction instead, and prove that, for any player satisfying a precisely defined richness condition on the group structure, it is the unique such map, up to a temperature parameter, satisfying five requirements. A sixth requirement fixes the sign of this temperature; a seventh, shown independent of the rest via an explicit counterexample, forces one shared temperature across all eligible players. A worked example on an exact cooperative game confirms the applicable requirements numerically and shows the construction degrades gracefully, valid but uninformative, when a player's evidence fails to distinguish between its groups.

papers.title: Risk aversion with two risks for state-dependent utilities
papers.title_ja: 状態依存効用における2つのリスク下のリスク回避
summary_ja: 主リスクに背景リスクが伴う状態依存効用の枠組みでアロー・プラットリスク回避を導入。
相関構造を考慮し、背景リスクの存在下で主リスクへのリスク回避性が保存される条件を導出。
一様リスク回避の概念を提案し、公正な保険契約や最適予防問題への応用を例示。
papers.reason_ja: 背景リスクが存在する状態依存選好でのリスク意思決定理論を拡張するため。
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the concept of Arrow-Pratt risk aversion within a two-attribute, state-dependent utility framework, where a primary risk is accompanied by a background risk. Within this setting, we investigate the interrelationships among risk aversion toward one risk in the presence of another risk, the structure of state-dependent two-attribute utility functions, and the degree of correlation between the two risks. More specifically, we establish conditions on the state-dependent two-attribute utility function under which risk aversion toward primary risk is preserved when a background risk is involved, considering various correlation structures between the two types of risks. Additionally, a new concept, uniform risk aversion in the presence of a background risk, is introduced. We show that the above established conditions on the state-dependent two-attribute utility function are equivalent to uniform risk aversion toward primary risk in presence of a background risk. These findings offer new insights into state-dependent preferences for correlated risks. Two applications in the contexts of fair insurance contract and optimal prevention within a two-period model illustrate the practical usefulness of the proposed risk aversion with two risks under state-dependent utilities.

papers.title: It Pays to Brag? On Counterfactual Fair Credit
papers.title_ja: 自慢する価値はあるか？反実仮想的な公平クレジット帰属について
summary_ja: 同一成果を得る複数の反実仮想的な方法を考慮できるようシャープレイ値を拡張。
効率性・無効性・劣モジュラ性の公平性公理が社会福祉最大化のインセンティブと相反することを示出。
劣モジュラ性を外すことで誘因整合的帰属が可能となり、古典的公理で標準値が一意に定まることを証明。
papers.reason_ja: シャープレイ値の反実仮想的拡張と公平性・誘因整合性のトレードオフを論じるため。
papers.abstract: Intellectual work, such as software, legal documents, and scientific results, typically builds on the work of others, and the same end product can often be obtained in several different ways. When assigning credit for such work, it is not clear whether credit should go according to the way the work was actually produced or also consider counterfactual ways of obtaining it. We study this question by generalizing Shapley values to account for counterfactual ways of obtaining the same result. We show that the fairness axioms of efficiency, nullity, and submodularity (in particular, additivity) are incompatible with incentivizing creators to maximize social welfare. In fact, fair credit can uniquely incentivize arbitrarily small welfare relative to the optimum. We also show that without submodularity, incentive compatibility is achievable, and that the four classical fairness axioms uniquely determine the Shapley value and prohibit dependence on counterfactual outcomes.

papers.title: Mechanism Design under Belief Disagreement: Allocation Flexibility and Rent Capacity
papers.title_ja: 信念の不一致下におけるメカニズムデザイン：割り当ての柔軟性とレント収容力
summary_ja: 買い手の競争に対する認識ズレに基づく単一主観法則下の分析。
割り当てが要求レントと収容力の双方を決定することを示した。
スコアと容量条件により大域的最適な下位財宝くじを特徴付け。
papers.reason_ja: 信念の不一致がメカニズムデザインのレント伝達に与える影響を学べるため。
papers.abstract: A seller jointly chooses allocation and payments when buyers misperceive competition. Under independent private values, statewise participation, and payment restrictions, allocation determines both required rents and their delivery capacity. We separate these effects under a common subjective law. For three values and shared-top beliefs, explicit score and capacity conditions characterize globally optimal lower-value lotteries, including top-rent overflow and welfare differences among revenue optima. A two-buyer construction establishes a strict allocation advantage over every reserve under the same fixed reporting certificate and positive margin. A transport test and exact band-boundary incentive equalities identify separate conditions restoring objective-law revenue ceilings. For three bands and a common affine belief interval, an explicitly certified reserve attains the ceiling under stated score conditions. A case scaled to public collectible-auction records yields a nominal shared-top allocation gain of 24.72 cents per auction. A one-cent report-by-report margin yields matched gains of 1.48 cents under projection and 3.32 cents under shared-top beliefs; the three-band point-belief gain of 2.50 cents disappears with common-interval protection. These comparisons bound the additional recurring costs an allocation redesign can cover at the specified reporting requirement.

papers.title: Subjective timing of information arrival
papers.title_ja: 情報到来の主観的タイミング
summary_ja: 本論文は情報の到来タイミングが主観的である状況を扱うと推測。
意思決定者が情報の時点をどう捉えるかモデル化していると推測。

papers.reason_ja: 意思決定理論における情報到来の主観的評価に関心がある読者に適する。

papers.title: Learning under Bounded Manipulation for Quadratic Incentive Design
papers.title_ja: 二乗インセンティブデザインにおける有界な操作の下での学習
summary_ja: リーダーが操作可能性のあるフォロワーのタイプを反復学習。
操作バジェット制約下でのミニマックスリグレット界を導出。
フォロワーの操作能力増加がリグレットを減らす逆説的現象を示す。
papers.reason_ja: 動的なインセンティブ設計と操作行動の下での学習理論を学べるため。
papers.abstract: We study a repeated quadratic incentive design game in which a leader learns a follower's private type from noisy observations of the follower's actions and uses her estimates in an affine incentive rule. The follower knows the leader's learning policy, which incorporates past observations to produce estimates of the follower's type, and can deviate from his myopic best response to influence the leader's future estimates. We ask how the follower's ability to manipulate these observations affects the leader's performance. Under a manipulation budget $C_T$ constraining the expected cumulative squared deviation of the follower's actions from his myopic best response, we establish a minimax regret rate of order $\max\{\log T, \min\{C_T,T\}\}$ for approximately rational followers. Our information-theoretic lower bound applies to a general class of causal estimation and manipulation policies for the leader and the follower. We provide a simple learning policy that achieves the lower bound. Finally, we show that under a fixed learning rule, increasing the manipulation budget of the follower can counterintuitively reduce the leader's regret.

papers.title: The Complexity of Fair and Stable Data Exchange
papers.title_ja: 公平で安定なデータ交換の計算複雑性
summary_ja: 相互性とコア安定性を満たすデータ交換の計算複雑性を解明。
劣モジュラ効用では近似相互かつ厳密コア安定な交換のFPTASを提案。
優モジュラ効用では近似解の導出であってもPPAD困難と証明。
papers.reason_ja: データ交換における公平性とコア安定性の計算限界を把握できるため。
papers.abstract: Data exchange is a fundamental challenge for Web applications such as recommender systems, personalized search, and fraud detection, where combining data across participants can improve predictions. Sustaining such collaboration requires fair returns for contributions and protection against groups leaving for a more beneficial exchange. These requirements are captured by reciprocity, which equates each participant's received utility with its credited contribution to others, and core stability, which rules out any coalition exchanging its own data to make every member strictly better off. Akrami et al. prove that such exchanges exist under broad assumptions, but leave efficient computation open. Two fundamental cases are submodular utilities, capturing diminishing returns from overlapping datasets, and supermodular utilities, capturing complementarities. We settle the approximate computation of reciprocal and core-stable exchanges in both cases, establishing a computational separation under Shapley sharing. For cross-monotone shares, which include Shapley shares under monotone submodular utilities, we give a circulation algorithm that computes an exactly core-stable, $ε$-reciprocal exchange in time poly$(n,1/ε,L)$ given efficient access to approximate shares, where $n$ is the number of participants and $L$ bounds how fast each donor's credit changes with its own contribution. This yields an FPTAS when $L$ is polynomially bounded. In contrast, finding an $ε$-reciprocal, $ε$-core-stable exchange is PPAD-hard for monotone lattice-supermodular utilities, even at inverse-polynomial accuracy, with constant $L$ and exact polynomial-time evaluation of Shapley shares. Thus overlapping information permits efficient fair and stable exchange, while complementarities create a computational barrier even when contribution credits are easy to evaluate.

papers.title: Logarithmic Tracing and Equilibrium Selection in Asymmetric Coordination Games
papers.title_ja: 非対称追従ゲームにおける対数トレーシングと均衡選択
summary_ja: 非対称純粋追従ゲームにおける対数正則化によるトレーシングを分析。
条件充足時に一様戦略からの均衡軌跡が単一の協調結果に収束。
2人ゲームでの平方根利得合計最大化則が3人以上では成立しない。
papers.reason_ja: 非対称ゲームでの均衡選択問題と対数トレーシング法を学べるため。
papers.abstract: We study equilibrium selection in asymmetric pure coordination games with finitely many players and actions. A logarithmic regularization defines a tracing-type path of interior equilibria from the uniform strategy profile. We reduce the equilibrium conditions to single-peaked scalar functions and show that, when one associated payoff index is uniquely minimal, the connected equilibrium branch from the uniform profile converges to the corresponding coordinated outcome. With two players, this condition is equivalent to maximizing the sum of square-root payoffs, extending the known two-action result to finitely many actions. A three-player example shows that the square-root rule does not generally extend to more players.

papers.title: Less Rational, More Transparent: Censorship as (Robustly) Optimal Disclosure
papers.title_ja: より低い合理性、より高い透明性：検閲としての（堅牢な）最適情報開示
summary_ja: ロジット量子応答に従う有界合理的ユーザーへの情報開示を分析。
合理性レベルが未知でも検閲（プール化）政策が堅牢に最適と証明。
合理性低下や不確実性増加には透明性を高める開示が最適と結論。
papers.reason_ja: 有界合理的意志決定者に対する堅牢な情報開示戦略を学べるため。
papers.abstract: Online platforms often control the information behind user decisions they want to influence, such as whether a driver accepts a trip or a buyer completes a purchase. A classical result in information disclosure shows that a {\em censorship} policy is optimal for the platform: the platform pools all sufficiently favorable options under a common message, such as a quality badge, and reveals the rest individually. This result, however, presumes fully rational users. We study disclosure to boundedly rational users who follow the logit quantal response model and whose rationality level the platform may not know. Our results deliver a unifying message: less rational, more transparent. Neither bounded rationality nor uncertainty about it calls for a more complex policy; each changes only how much the platform should pool, and only toward greater transparency. When the rationality level is known, censorship remains optimal, and less rational users optimally receive at least as much information as more rational ones. When the rationality level is unknown, censorship remains robustly optimal under each of three criteria: the maximin ratio, maximin payoff, and minimax regret, and the robust censorship can be chosen to be at least as transparent as the policy designed for fully rational users. This additional transparency weakly benefits both parties and acts as insurance against behavioral uncertainty: rationality-robust censorship secures at least 89.96\% of the payoff attainable with knowledge of the user's rationality level, whereas the policy designed for fully rational users can secure as little as 50\%. Taken together, these results suggest that platforms can keep their badge-based disclosure but should narrow its coverage when users may be boundedly rational.

papers.title_ja: 私的容量を持つ最大流におけるメカニズムデザイン
summary_ja: ネットワークの容量情報が私的情報である状況を扱うと推測。
プレイヤーの虚偽申告を防ぐメカニズムデザインを議論と推測。
効率的な最大流の達成とインセンティブ実効性の両立を分析と推測。
papers.reason_ja: ネットワーク型リソース配分とインセンティブ設計を学べるため。

papers.title: Eliminating Make-Whole Uplifts with a Minimum-Cost Uniform Price Adder
papers.title_ja: 最小コスト一律価格加算器による補填支払いの排除
summary_ja: エネルギーとランプ予備力の共同最適化における補填支払いを分析。
補填支払いを不要にする一律追加価格LMP+Uを提案。
送電線混雑下での需要家支払いを最小化し局所的誠実入札を保証。
papers.reason_ja: 電力市場デザインにおけるインセンティブ適合的な価格設定を学べる。
papers.abstract: Co-optimizing energy and flexible ramping reserves may dispatch generators at locational marginal prices (LMPs) below their submitted energy offer prices, necessitating out-of-market make-whole payments. Such payments create discriminatory settlements among generators and may incentivize strategic bidding for higher profits. This paper proposes LMP+U, an in-market uniform price adder to LMP for transmission-constrained networks, which minimizes demand payments subject to zero out-of-market make-whole uplift, preserves LMP-based congestion charges, and provides locally truthful bidding incentives for price-taking generators. We also identify conditions under which a price-taking generator can increase its profit by inflating its energy offer under conventional LMP with make-whole uplift. Numerical simulations illustrate the properties of LMP+U and its advantages over conventional LMP in congested networks.

papers.title: Epistemic Social Learning: Latent Behavioral Structure under Endogenous Multi-Agent Interaction
papers.title_ja: 内生的なマルチエージェント相互作用における潜在的行動構造と認識的社会学習
summary_ja: 他者の行動を推定する学習において対戦相手の変更に適応する認識的社会学習（ESL）を提案した。
高速なベイズ信念更新と緩やかなプロトタイプ学習を結合し、意思決定と観察の相互作用を定式化した。
12種類のゲーム等の実験で、ESLが既存の潜在適応手法の中で最も低いスイッチ後後悔量を達成した。
papers.reason_ja: 相手の戦略変化に対する信念更新と意思決定の相互作用に関心がある研究者に有用。
papers.abstract: In multi-agent interaction, a learner's actions shape the observations from which it infers other agents' behavior. A behavioral model may predict these observations well yet support poor adaptation when opponents change. We introduce Epistemic Social Learning (ESL), which couples fast, interaction-specific Bayesian beliefs with slower online learning of population-shared behavioral prototypes. Belief-conditioned decisions influence subsequent observations and, in turn, the representations learned from them. Under explicit regularity and averaging assumptions, we provide a conditional stochastic-approximation characterization of these coupled dynamics. Across twelve synthetic $3\times3$ cooperative, coordination, and adversarial games, ESL achieves the lowest aggregate post-switch regret among the evaluated online latent-adaptation methods, including a switch-aware Bayesian filter. Additional experiments examine observation loss, noise, and asymmetric incentives. These findings illustrate how predictive fit can differ from decision-relevant adaptation under policy-dependent interaction.

papers.title: Stinespring's Dilation, Universal-NOT, and Limitations of Quantum Uncoupled Learning
papers.title_ja: スティーンスプリングの可張定理、ユニバーサルNOT、および量子非結合学習の限界
summary_ja: プレイヤーが自身の利得のみを知る非結合学習の量子版における、ナッシュ均衡への収束限界を解析した。
共役ゲームにおいて記憶を持たない自律的な量子ダイナミクスがナッシュ均衡に収束しないことを証明した。
小規模な古典メモリで収束可能になる一方、有限メモリでは全量子状態の連続体に対応できないことを示した。
papers.reason_ja: 量子ゲーム理論や分散学習ダイナミクスにおける均衡収束の理論的限界に興味がある研究者に適する。
papers.abstract: Uncoupled learning, in which players know only their own payoff, are a standard model of decentralized learning toward Nash equilibrium. We study their quantum counterpart, where strategies are quantum states and, in each round, a player receives a physical copy of their opponent's current strategy and updates their own state by a quantum channel. This adds to uncoupledness a constraint with no classical analogue: every update must be physically realizable. In fact, this constraint is decisive in conjugation games, in which Bob has a strictly dominant pure strategy and Alice's unique best response is its transpose. In this work, we show some limitations of uncoupled (learning) dynamics in finding the Nash equilibrium for conjugation games. First, we prove that no autonomous, memoryless, uncoupled dynamics converge to Nash equilibrium in a family of four single-qubit conjugation games. Specifically, any memoryless channel that keeps all four equilibria fixed will leave Alice's strategy frozen. This result also extends to $4^n$ games on $n$-qubit registers. Second, we show that this barrier disappears with a small classical memory: for any finite family of $L$ pure targets, a guess-and-test rule with $O(\log L)$ classical bits converges to equilibrium, with an explicit bound on its convergence rate. Finally, we prove that no finite memory, classical or quantum, suffices for the continuum of all pure-qubit targets. Our proof of the impossibility for memoryless channels relies on Stinespring's dilation theorem, while the impossibility for finite-memory channels relies on the optimal universal-NOT (in)fidelity bound by Bužek, Hillery, and Werner.

papers.title: Stackelberg Games with Convex Risk Measures

summary_ja: 環境の不確実性から生じる利得を、各プレイヤーが凸リスク測度で評価するシュタッケルベルクゲームを分析した。

papers.reason_ja: 不確実性下の意思決定モデルやリスク考慮型ゲーム理論の均衡概念・計算に関心のある読者に適する。
papers.abstract: Stackelberg games have important real-world applications in which reliable commitments require accounting for multiple sources of uncertainty. We study finite Stackelberg games in which environmental uncertainty makes each mixed strategy profile induce a random reward, and each player evaluates that reward with a convex monetary risk criterion. In reward form, it is a concave, monotone, translation-equivariant utility and also represented as penalized expected reward over distributions of environmental outcomes. We provide two conditions under which the follower has a unique continuous mixed response, which leads to inducible optimistic equilibrium. We show that even approximate equilibrium computation is NP Hard. We then derive an exact mathematical program with equilibrium constraints for the problem. We also develop an action entropy smoothed implicit-gradient method and prove an end-to-end additive approximation guarantee under the assumption that the gradient method reaches global optimality. We validate our scalability and other results with experiments on synthetic and real data.

papers.title: Last-Iterate Convergence of Payoff-Gradient Learning in Möbius Pricing Games

summary_ja: 第一価格オークション等を含むベイズ型ゲームにおける利得勾配学習の全域的な最終反復収束を証明した。

papers.abstract: We prove global last-iterate convergence of payoff-gradient learning in every typewise Riemannian metric, which for scalar actions is the same as typewise mirror descent, with explicit rates, in a class of Bayesian bidding and pricing games that includes first-price auctions, unit-demand pay-as-bid auctions, rank-based generalized first-price auctions, and homogeneous-good price competition with inelastic demand. The result holds for symmetric self-play: all players use a common strategy and apply the same payoff-gradient update at each type. Convergence is from every continuous weakly increasing feasible initial strategy, including pooling, and does not rely on the monotonicity or Minty conditions that underlie existing guarantees in other games. Instead, the class is characterized by two structural properties: a direct payoff effect that is independent of the action, and a payoff difference at the allocation threshold that is affine in the action. These properties reduce the learning dynamics to a singular transport-damping equation for the common strategy, which, under the stated coefficient and metric assumptions, admits a unique viscosity solution. Comparison barriers make the uniform distance to the unique rest point a strict Lyapunov functional and yield convergence rates with optimal algebraic exponents. In allocation games, the rest point is the unique weakly increasing symmetric equilibrium under the stated tie-breaking conditions, and a positive lower slope bound converts strategy-error bounds into explicit approximate-equilibrium guarantees. A projected grid scheme with a slope floor makes the approximation constructive, with error bounds under deterministic perturbations and almost-sure convergence on a fixed grid under martingale gradient noise.

summary_ja: 移植数tをパラメータとする腎臓交換問題に対し、決定論的なO*(4^{t+o(t)})時間アルゴリズムを開発した。

papers.abstract: Kidney exchange admits a randomized $O^*(4^t)$ algorithm parameterized by the target number $t$ of transplants, but the best previous deterministic algorithm requires $O^*(6.855^t)$ time. We nearly close this gap by developing a deterministic $O^*(4^{t+o(t)})$ algorithm. Our approach uses Dynamic Representative Sets to execute the semi-feasible packing recurrence under a global cardinality budget of $2t$, exploiting a residual extension-budget invariant to avoid repeated static representative-family compression. To handle admissible cycles containing at least $t$ vertices, we establish a deterministic $O^*(4^{k+o(k)})$ algorithm for finding a shortest simple directed cycle of length at least $k$. Beyond feasibility, our framework supports additive optimization, yielding the same running-time bound for maximizing arc utility among packings with exactly $t$ transplants. Consequently, a packing that lexicographically maximizes the number of transplants and then additive utility can be computed deterministically in $O^*(4^{τ+o(τ)})$ time, where $τ$ is the maximum achievable number of transplants.

papers.abstract: The paper analyzes, by means of a theoretical model of two‐stage college study, the effects of two kinds of tuition subsidies, unconditional tuition discounts versus dropout‐contingent forgiveness of student loans. Students' imperfect knowledge of their academic ability at the time of matriculation and its updating in the course of study are factors in their responses to funding policies. Mitigating the resulting risk in college attendance is the rationale for government intervention by means of tuition subsidies. We find that while unconditional tuition subsidies incentivize both matriculation and continued study even upon the revelation of low ability and hence low returns to college, partial forgiveness of student debt conditional on dropping out maintains incentives to matriculate but adds option value by relieving a part of sunk tuition debt when evaluating a decision to persist in college. It thus reduces the incentives to do so when low future returns are revealed. We show that this policy is superior in terms of mitigating the “bad debt” held by students, that unrecouped by returns to college. Moreover, a budget‐neutral conversion of a part of unconditional tuition subsidy to targeted debt forgiveness increases aggregate net productivity gain due to college education and reduces the aggregate bad debt held by students.

Social scientists and research can play a powerful role in shaping policy. Early Career grants and the grantee resources that accompany them are intended to support early career scholars looking to advance their academic careers, as well as engage with nonacademic audiences. Grantees will have the opportunity to participate in trainings and receive assistance in translating research findings for nonacademic audiences. Our goal is to help equip an academic network with the necessary skills and opportunities to shape public debates and policy outcomes, including via temporary government service. Therefore, we place particular value on applications from scholars who exhibit willingness and ability to engage with media and policymakers on their research. Research generated by the scholars supported in response to this Request for Proposals will have the potential to generate actionable insights. This includes research that illuminates the policies that help or hinder more equitable growth in the United States, as well as research that identifies the need for a policy response. We support scholars from across academic disciplines whose research relies on a variety of methodological approaches. Research agendas should relate to the broad areas of the economy described below. inequality.abstract: Key takeaways U.S. policymakers need to prepare our nation’s workforce for the potential for job dislocation posed by the rise of artificial intelligence, and this should begin now, even as the outlook remains highly uncertain. To assist those impacted by AI dislocation, policies should not target only those who can prove AI-caused job loss, but instead offer supports that are universally available for all displaced workers, including universal job search assistance and universal income support for workers in transition. Instead of succumbing to “training nihilism” that generalizes past weaknesses of the overall training system, policymakers should invest in specific workforce development strategies that have shown success alongside innovation and improved data. Broader options are needed for workers who lose their jobs, including expanded, progressive wage insurance that can complement workforce training. Policymakers should pursue “automatic scaling-up” strategies in addition to automatic stabilizers to ensure we are able to quickly and effectively accelerate responses to labor market challenges as they evolve. Innovation is needed around policies that discourage unnecessary layoffs, including by supporting redeployment and shorter workweeks without reductions in pay. Alongside other needed measures to support worker power and create good jobs, these policies would support economic dignity for workers amid the potential turbulence of an AI transition, while helping ensure that the gains of productivity growth are more equitably shared. Overview and summary The rise of artificial intelligence and the potential for new technology to spark widespread job dislocation reflects a unique challenge for policymakers because of how wide the range of scenarios might be for the depth, breadth and speed of displacement. Economists and technologists have suggested possibilities that range from a transition that is challenging for a subset of workers but in line with prior technological advances to much more dramatic disruptions that dislocate tens of millions of workers, end career paths that previously felt reliable and even lead to a net reduction of jobs with gains concentrated among a relative few. Our report argues that under almost any scenario, the United States will need a major expansion of worker adjustment policies and that efforts to build those policies should begin now, even as the outlook remains highly uncertain. The United States lags far behind peer nations in having the basic infrastructure today to help support workers who face the potential of AI-induced job dislocation as they transition into new, successful career paths. If you’d like to opt out of columns, or any other section, you can do so here . The notion of biotech hedge funds always felt a little strange to me. Yes, hedge funds are filled with clever people with clever ideas, like trading brick-and-mortar stocks based on satellite imagery showing how many cars are in their parking lots, but how are you going to trade on clinical trial results? Start up a lab? Whether drugs work in humans feels as unpredictable as anything else in biology. Maybe you can depend on the base rate of how often drugs for a particular disease area are approved, but everyone knows that already. Surely there are no dollar bills on the ground here waiting to be picked up. And yet, hundreds of billions of dollars are managed by hedge funds and investment firms that specialize in biotech. The largest are Baker Brothers Advisors, Deerfield Management, and OrbiMed, each managing over $15 billion. Below them sit dozens more. How can these funds, some of which have been around for decades, possibly know more than the people doing the science? Well, a surprisingly large number of clinical trial results are actually decently predictable by anyone willing to simply look. Some very expensive trials are run for seemingly no reason at all, all of which have failed incredibly badly in the past and have little reason to succeed in the future. LLMs may have replaced a decent chunk of the work here, but, in the past, hiring a small army of graduate students to compile information was table stakes for any self-respecting hedge fund. One of the most famous of the pack – RA Capital – has an entire division called ‘ TechAtlas ’ dedicated to the effort. But we needn’t rely on LLMs or human ingenuity for this! Insilico Medicine has published a paper on inClinico , a platform that predicts Phase II clinical trial outcomes using embarrassingly simple inputs: ‘target choice’ features (whether this is a good drug for this disease, based on omics data and a biomedical knowledge graph) and ‘trial design’ features (like enrollment size, blinding, number of endpoints, patient age, location, and funder type). Their predictions, which were date-stamped and published on preprint servers before the trials read out, hit 79 percent accuracy across 14 resolved trials. But then we arrive at the same problem as before: if it’s as easy as training a model or a human on what is essentially public information, how does anybody make money here? Sometimes the answer is private information. The biotech investing industry spends enormous sums on paid consultations with expert networks. The business model is straightforward. An analyst at a biotech hedge fund wants to understand whether a particular clinical trial is likely to succeed. They pay an expert network $500 to $1,000 or more per hour to connect them with an individual who treats the disease in question, or who has run similar trials, or sits on advisory boards, or is otherwise an ‘expert’. The analyst asks questions, and the expert answers. The stated purpose is to gain non-obvious insights. All of this is perfectly above board . There is no legal apparatus that prevents you from staring deeply into a clinician’s glassy eyes and asking them whether the trial’s endpoint is well chosen. There is nothing stopping you from taking their moment of hesitation as a sign of something worth trading on. It is a friendly conversation, and the SEC cannot prevent you from making friends. signals.abstract: “Unprecedented” is how Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky described his country’s successful operation that brought down parts of the Kerch Bridge earlier this month. The connector between mainland Russia and occupied Crimea has been a key Ukrainian target since the start of the war, for both its strategic and symbolic importance to Putin’s rule. It wasn’t just the Kremlin that Kyiv was sending a message to, however. What made the operation even more impressive is that virtually all of it was conducted using homegrown Ukrainian – and in two cases, European – drones and missiles . It did not rely on Starlink either. Ukraine’s access to the satellite system, which is run by Elon Musk’s SpaceX, has in recent weeks been throttled on multiple occasions, compromising the nation’s war efforts. With the attack, Ukraine showed that it also held cards – and did not necessarily need Washington to play them. The episode is a textbook case of what countries can achieve when necessity breeds innovation. It also shows the downside of overzealously weaponising dependencies: those on the receiving end will be spurred to look for alternatives – and will eventually find them. Europe, which has also been working to reduce its dependency on US technology, would do well to learn from this example. This is not the first time that Ukraine’s dependency on Starlink has proved fragile. In February 2025, in the lead-up to Zelensky’s infamous visit to the White House, the Trump administration reportedly suggested that Ukraine would lose Starlink access if it didn’t sign on to its disadvantageous critical mineral deal. In response, European capitals rushed to find alternatives that they could offer Kyiv. They soon found that they had few on offer: Starlink, and its US military-governed version Starshield, remains by far the most mature and cutting-edge solution when it comes to this type of space-based connectivity. Europe’s own challengers in this domain, such as Franco-British Eutelsat, had long struggled to compete and lacks the reach to offer a like-for-like replacement. And scaling these alternatives would take time. When Musk finally appeared to have made good on Trump’s threat this October, Europe was far from ready to fully fill the void, though it had made progress. With access to Starshield still restricted, Ukraine’s military has been relying on a patchwork of Eutelsat and other European solutions. For its attack on the Kerch Bridge, Ukraine took an even more MacGyverian approach, deploying relay drones that were mounted with radios and modems. While these solutions are certainly no Starshield, they work on Ukraine’s own terms. The 2025 Starlink incident became an important catalyst for Europe’s longer-term ambitions to become less dependent on US technology. The worry across the bloc is that meddling with Kyiv’s access could just as easily happen to Paris, Rome or Berlin. signals.abstract: When architect Paul Williams first entered the site of the new London Museum a decade ago, it felt like walking into a time capsule. The old Smithfield General Market in the city’s central Farringdon neighbourhood had ceased trading 20 years before. “There were the trolleys, meat hooks, ledgers,” he says. “Calendars marked. Life suddenly left and traders just moved out. There was a ghostly feeling of that presence still there.” He pauses. “It was very moving.” Ghosts in the architecture remain today. Multiple levels of shops and offices around the market’s periphery have been removed but there are still the cavities where the beams that supported them once lay. The brickwork is blackened in places and tinged blue in others – vestiges of historic office partitions and wall coverings. The fireplaces have been removed, meticulously restored and then reinstated in their original positions; they hang high and spectral above the new ground level. Dwarfed by the cavernous space, they resemble iron postage stamps – relics of the market’s past life and history’s storytellers in its new one. From left: Architects Lyall Thow from Julian Harrap, Paul Williams from Stanton Williams and Asif Khan in the vaults Given its purpose, the structure – part of a complex designed and built by architect Horace Jones between 1879 and 1883 – inspires an unlikely awe. The great, soaring dome in the heart of the ceiling evokes a cathedral-like reverence. Wrought-iron berries and leaves decorate the top of the Phoenix columns that dot the vast floor. Originally designed for fruit and vegetables, the space was repurposed as a place to sell fish, before becoming a meat market in 1898. For more than a century, this building was the heart of London’s meat trade: somewhere that came alive at night as crowds of men strung up sides of pork and heaved carcasses over their shoulders. When Monocle visits in early November, Smithfield is once again bustling with activity. Bloodstained white coats have been replaced by hard hats and hi-vis; shanks and ribs with spirit levels and scaffolding poles. The project is designed by architecture firm Stanton Williams with collaborating architect Asif Khan and conservation architects Julian Harrap, and the site’s transformation from 19th-century trade hall into the biggest city museum in the world is almost complete. When visitors arrive, they will likely enter on West Poultry Avenue, a street that has now been enclosed by the museum. Here, data about London will be shared in real time. On one side of the street is the Poultry Market, which will open as part of London Museum in 2028. On the other is the magnificent, domed General Market, home to the Our Time galleries, which display objects that pertain to living memory. Beneath it is the subterranean Past Time section, inhabiting what was once a railway goods depot that helped to streamline the market’s operations. Past Time tells the story of London from prehistory to 2012, when the city hosted the Olympic and Paralympic Games. ruscn.abstract: Год назад, 24 ноября 2025 года, свои двери открыла современная SMART-поликлиника Якутской городской больницы №2. Новое учреждение, построенное в рамках государственно-частного партнерства, стало ключевым звеном здравоохранения города. За год поликлиника приняла более 264 тысяч пациентов. Это тысячи спасенных жизней, вовремя поставленных диагнозов и начатых курсов лечения, сообщает Минздрав Якутии. «Я вожу сюда и ребенка, и хожу сама. Отдельные входы – это гениально, никто никому не мешает. Врачи внимательные, а благодаря новой системе навигации даже пожилые люди легко находят нужные кабинеты. Теперь диспансеризация для всей семьи занимает не недели, а пару визитов», – поблагодарила многодетная мама Саргылана Иванова. «Раньше, чтобы пройти всех врачей, нужно было потратить два дня и объехать полгорода. Теперь все здесь, в одном светлом здании. Записалась через Госуслуги, пришла к своему времени, прошла обследование. Это совершенно другой уровень», – сказала якутянка Марина. Работа по модернизации первичного звена здравоохранения в республике проводится во исполнение целей и задач национального проекта «Продолжительная и активная жизнь», инициированного президентом страны Владимиром Путиным. «Открытие Смарт-поликлиники ЯГБ №2 – это яркий пример успешной реализации нацпроекта «Продолжительная и активная жизнь». Мы видим не просто стены и оборудование, а работающую экосистему, где во главе угла стоят время и комфорт пациента. Результаты первого года – 264 тысячи принятых пациентов и высший балл по Стандарту СТИМУЛ – говорят сами за себя. Это ориентир для всей системы здравоохранения Якутии», – отметила министр здравоохранения Якутии Лена Афанасьева. Фото: Минздрав Якутии Новый медицинский центр в Гагаринском округе рассчитан на 600 посещений в смену. Условия, в которых ранее работала больница, не соответствовали современным требованиям здравоохранения. Еще в 2019 году главой республики Айсеном Николаевым было принято решение о строительстве нового поликлинического здания в рамках развития города Якутска. Сегодня в SMART-поликлинике на площади около девяти тысяч квадратных метров разместились женская консультация на 120 посещений, дневной стационар, диагностические и терапевтические отделения, отделения лучевой диагностики и восстановительного лечения, клинико-диагностическая лаборатория, кабинеты неотложной помощи и стоматологии. «Благодаря новой системе навигации и разделению потоков, мы можем уделять больше времени непосредственно лечению, а не административной работе. Электронные карты и современное диагностическое оборудование российского производства позволяют ставить диагнозы в день обращения. Это колоссальная экономия времени и для врача, и для пациента», – говорят врачи Якутской городской больницы №2. Инфраструктура SMART-поликлиники продумана до мелочей: отдельные входы для взрослых, детей и пациенток женской консультации, просторные помещения и интуитивная навигация. Объект оснащен более 700 единицами современного оборудования, около 70% из которого – российского производства, включая аппараты МРТ, КТ и экспертного класса УЗИ, что позволяет проводить полный цикл обследований в одном месте. А внедрение электронных медкарт, запись через колл-центр 122 и автоматические напоминания свели время на организационные вопросы к минимуму.
